recipes.label: Neutral Baseline
keyCues: Relaxed forehead and brow arch
Eyelids resting naturally over the upper iris margin
Lips lightly closed without corner tension or chin dimpling

recipes.label: Happiness (Duchenne Smile)
recipes.eyesLids: Cheeks raised, crow's feet, lower lid pushed up
recipes.noseMouthJaw: Lip corners pulled up and back
keyCues: AU6 (Cheek Raiser) pushes the cheeks up and crinkles crow's feet at the outer eye corners
AU12 (Lip Corner Puller) curves the mouth corners upward and back toward the cheekbones
Lower eyelids bag slightly as the orbicularis oculi contracts

recipes.label: Social / Posed Smile (AU12 Only)
recipes.eyesLids: Wide and uncrinkled; no cheek raise or crow's feet
recipes.noseMouthJaw: Lip corners pulled up by zygomaticus major alone
keyCues: Mouth corners pull upward (AU12), but the upper cheeks and eye corners remain completely relaxed
Absence of AU6 crow's-feet wrinkles and lower-lid elevation
In dynamic timelines, social smiles often step on and off abruptly

recipes.label: Low Amusement (Subtle Duchenne)
keyCues: Symmetrical low-intensity smile (AU12) paired with soft cheek elevation (AU6)
Bilateral symmetry distinguishes it from unilateral contempt (AU14)

recipes.label: Sadness (Full with Chin Raise)
recipes.browsForehead: Inner corners raised and drawn together (oblique)
recipes.noseMouthJaw: Lip corners down, chin pushed up
keyCues: AU1 + AU4 lift the inner eyebrow corners and draw them together into an oblique triangle
AU15 pulls the lip corners distinctly downward
AU17 pushes the chin boss upward, arching the lower lip

recipes.label: Sadness (Without Chin Raise)
keyCues: Oblique inner brows (AU1 + AU4) with depressed lip corners (AU15)
Chin boss remains flatter without AU17 mentalis contraction

recipes.label: Anger (Pressed Lips)
recipes.browsForehead: Lowered and pulled together, vertical lines
recipes.eyesLids: Hard stare, upper lid raised, lower lid tense
recipes.noseMouthJaw: Lips pressed thin or squared open
keyCues: AU4 strongly lowers the brows and draws them together with vertical glabella furrows
AU5 + AU7 create a focused, hard stare (upper lid raised while lower lid tenses)
AU23 + AU24 tighten and press the lips into a thin, tense line

recipes.label: Fear
recipes.browsForehead: Raised AND pulled together, flat or wavy line
recipes.eyesLids: Upper whites visible, lower lid tense
recipes.noseMouthJaw: Lips stretched horizontally; mouth nearly closed
keyCues: AU1 + AU2 + AU4 (at 0.85) raise and pinch the brows together into a flatter, straighter horizontal line than surprise
AU5 exposes white sclera above the iris while AU7 tenses the lower lid
AU20 pulls the lips wide horizontally toward the ears with the jaw nearly closed (AU26 <= 0.10), never the relaxed 'O' of surprise

recipes.label: Surprise
recipes.browsForehead: Raised high and curved, long horizontal lines
keyCues: AU1 + AU2 arch the entire eyebrows high and curved without any medial AU4 pinch
AU5 opens the eyes wide with relaxed lower lids (no AU7 squint)
AU26 drops the jaw into a relaxed, oval open mouth without AU20 horizontal stretch

recipes.label: Disgust (Full)
recipes.browsForehead: Lowered slightly by nasal bridge pull
keyCues: AU9 wrinkles the bridge and sides of the nose and pulls the medial brow down
AU10 pulls the upper lip upward into an inverted-U arch, deepening the upper nasolabial fold
Distinguished from anger by nasal bridge wrinkling and upper-lip elevation rather than thin pressed lips

recipes.label: Disgust (Nose Wrinkle + Upper Lip)
keyCues: Pure AU9 (Nose Wrinkler) + AU10 (Upper Lip Raiser) without lower-lip depression
Concentrated in the nasal bridge and upper nasolabial furrow

recipes.label: Contempt (Right Unilateral AU14)
recipes.noseMouthJaw: One lip corner tightened and raised
keyCues: Unilateral AU14 (Dimpler) tightens and slightly lifts only one corner of the mouth
The only Ekman basic expression defined by strict left/right asymmetry
Eyes remain neutral, distinguishing it from bilateral amusement (AU6 + AU12)

recipes.label: Contempt (Left Unilateral AU14)
keyCues: Unilateral AU14 on the subject's left mouth corner
Asymmetrical dimple and corner tightening without cheek raise

recipes.label: Physical / Empathetic Pain
keyCues: Brows strongly lowered (AU4) while cheeks raise (AU6) and lids tighten hard (AU7)
Nose wrinkles (AU9) and lips part under tension (AU25)

recipes.label: Concentration / Focus
keyCues: Knitted brows (AU4) and slight lid tightening (AU7) while the mouth remains completely relaxed
Easy to misread as mild anger if context (reading, problem-solving) is ignored

recipes.label: Skepticism / Doubt
keyCues: Unilateral outer brow raise (AU2 on one side) paired with chin raise (AU17)
Communicates questioning or evaluating a claim

recipes.label: Embarrassment
keyCues: Gaze shifts downward, head pitches down (-10 deg) and turns slightly away
Controlled, sheepish smile (low AU12 pressed with AU24) and often a hand-to-face/neck gesture

recipes.label: Shame
keyCues: Head drops steeply (-20 deg), gaze averted downward, slumped/collapsed shoulders
Sad lower-face tension (AU15 + AU17) without the controlled smile of embarrassment

recipes.label: Pride
keyCues: Chin tilts upward (+10 deg head pitch), expanded chest posture
Small, composed smile (AU12 at 0.3-0.4)

recipes.label: Terror / Horror (AU27 Mouth Stretch)
keyCues: Extreme fear brow pinch (AU1+2+4) and wide eyes (AU5) combined with active jaw stretch (AU27) and horizontal pull (AU20)

confusablePairs.title: Fear vs. Surprise
confusablePairs.keyCue: Fear pulls the brows together and stretches the lips. Surprise has curved, raised brows and a relaxed open jaw.
confusablePairs.explanation: In fear, AU4 pulls the raised brows inward so they look flatter and tense, while AU20 pulls the mouth horizontally with the jaw nearly closed (AU26 <= 0.10). In surprise, AU1+2 arch high without AU4, and AU26 drops the jaw into a relaxed oval.

confusablePairs.title: Anger vs. Disgust
confusablePairs.keyCue: Anger shows in the brows and lips. Disgust shows in the nose and upper lip.
confusablePairs.explanation: Anger lowers the brows with a hard stare (AU4+5+7) and presses the lips thin (AU23+24). Disgust wrinkles the nasal bridge (AU9) and raises the upper lip into an inverted-U arch (AU10).

confusablePairs.title: Sadness vs. Fear
confusablePairs.keyCue: Both raise the inner brow. Sadness drops the lip corners. Fear stretches the lips and widens the eyes.
confusablePairs.explanation: Both share AU1+4 in the medial brow, but sadness droops the upper lids and pulls the lip corners down (AU15 + AU17 chin raise), whereas fear widens the upper lids (AU5) and stretches the lips horizontally (AU20).

confusablePairs.title: Genuine (Duchenne) vs. Social Smile
confusablePairs.keyCue: Check the eyes (AU6), symmetry and timing. Fake smiles start and stop abruptly.
confusablePairs.explanation: A genuine Duchenne smile engages AU6 (orbicularis oculi), lifting the cheeks, pushing up the lower lids, and crinkling crow's feet. A social smile activates only AU12 (zygomaticus major) in the lower face.

confusablePairs.title: Contempt vs. Amusement
confusablePairs.keyCue: Contempt is one-sided and does not involve the eyes.
confusablePairs.explanation: Contempt is a unilateral AU14 dimpler tightening on one mouth corner only, with neutral eyes. Low amusement is bilateral (both mouth corners rise via AU12) with subtle cheek elevation (AU6).
